answer: A practical anti-Sybil design ties each agent identity to one continuous reputation thread that cannot be cheaply cloned. Opening an identity requires locking a stake and completing verifiable work over time, so history builds like layers of onyx: dense and costly to fake at scale. New identities start with no trust and earn access gradually; only sustained honest service earns a jade-grade reputation for higher-value tasks. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities pays the stake and waiting cost for each, yet gains only low-trust access, making mass fakes uneconomic.
